To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adipose tissue‐ derived mesenchymal stem cells (AT‐MSCs) were recruited into prostate tumors by prostate cancer cells, and that these AT‐MSCs promoted tumor growth.
the adipose tissue‐associated stromal cells are recruited by the prostate cancer cells, and that the adipose‐derived stem cells are recruited by prostate cancer cells and help tumor growth.

the adipose tissue‐associated stromal cells (ASCs), including adipose tissue‐mesenchymal stem cells (ASC‐MSCs) and adipose tissue‐fibroblasts (ASC‐FBs), are recruited by prostate cancer cells and that ASC‐MSCs and ASC‐FBs promote tumor progression by enhancing tumor angiogenesis and inhibiting the host immunity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of adipose tissue and its stem cells in the pathogenesis of prostate cancer.
the effects of adipose tissue-derived stem cells (ADSCs) on prostate cancer.
the effects of transplantation of adipocyte‐derived stem cells in prostate tumor, which may help us understand the mechanism of obesity in the occurrence of prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of stem cells in the treatment of prostate cancer has not yet been proven to be effective.
obesity is a risk factor of prostate cancer, but the underlying mechanisms are not fully understood and need further investigation.
adipose tissue-derived MSCs can be a promising cell source for tissue engineering applications in urology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adipose tissue‐ derived stem cells (ASC) can be recruited to the prostate cancer site and promote prostate tumor growth.

adipose tissue‐ derived stem cells (ASCs) are recruited by prostate tumor cells to promote tumor growth and that the tumor‐associated ASCs promote the growth of prostate tumor cells through the paracrine action of the secreted factors, including interleukin‐6 and transforming growth factor‐β1.
the obesity‐associated adipose tissue‐associated stromal cells are recruited to the tumor site and contribute to the growth and progression of prostate cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
obesity is associated with an increased risk of developing prostate cancer.
obesity is associated with a higher risk of prostate cancer, and that this may be related to the recruitment of adipose tissue stromal cells by the tumor.
obesity increases the risk of prostate cancer development by increasing the number of adipose tissue-derived stromal cells, which in turn, increase the risk of prostate tumor development.
